what_it_does: It shows the reader one real team, one real edit and its measured win rates before or beside the general claim, so the claim has something concrete to stand on.
when_to_use: Right after Rami says he measures whether one edit changes the win rate by more than noise, so the reader sees a big edit, a tiny edit and an unchanged repeat side by side.
sentence_pattern: Take team x. Change y to z. Its win rate moves from a to b. Battled again with nothing changed, it scores c, d and e.
anchor_in_draft: If change greater than noise it change it hard.

candidates.sentence: Take one tournament-ready team: Raichu, Staraptor, Garchomp, Charizard, Gholdengo and Sylveon. It won 56.25% of 384 battles against the 50 top-placing teams. Swap Charizard for a real Mawile set from another team and it wins 43.49%. Battle the unchanged team three more times and it scores 52.34%, 53.12% and 52.86%. One example carries about 3.4 points of battle luck, so it illustrates the measurement and proves nothing on its own.

facts.claim: Starting team a09, from MB20.txt, has Raichu, Staraptor, Garchomp, Charizard, Gholdengo and Sylveon.
a09 scored 0.5625 over 384 battles, 216 wins, and its three replays scored 0.5234, 0.5312 and 0.5286.
Edit m09_F0 replaces Charizard @ Charizardite Y with Mawile @ Mawilite, Hyper Cutter, Iron Head, Play Rough, Rock Slide, Sucker Punch, copied from a real set.
Two scores of the same unchanged team differ by about 3.40 points for tournament-ready teams.
The same team and edits appear in the issue #313 storyboard, frames 2 and 4.

candidates.sentence: On the same team, change only the item Charizard holds, from Charizardite Y to Miracle Seed, and its win rate drops from 56.25% to 45.57%. Charizardite Y is a Mega Stone, the item that lets Charizard Mega Evolve, so this random edit takes away Charizard's Mega Evolution. About a quarter of the item edits in the study remove a Mega Stone, and that may be one reason item edits move win rate as much as they do, a guess we have not tested.

facts.claim: Edit a09_C0 changes Charizard @ Charizardite Y to Charizard @ Miracle Seed and nothing else.
a09_C0 scored 0.4557 over 384 battles. The starting team scored 0.5625.
32 of the 120 item edits remove a Mega Stone, such as Floettite, Charizardite Y or Raichunite Y.
facts.source: count of removed items over ~/vgc-data/edit_kind_rerun/teams/ruggedness/a??_C?.txt and ~/vgc-data/edit_kind_rerun/teams/ruggedness2/s??_C?.txt against their starting teams, 2026-11-13; v2/FACTS.md, 'Scope limits'

facts.claim: Item edits are random legal values, not the edits a player or a search would choose.
That a lost Mega Stone explains part of the item-edit size is a hypothesis. The study did not split item edits by Mega Stone.
facts.source: no source; marked as a hypothesis

candidates.sentence: Now change one of Raichu's moves, Nuzzle to Volt Tackle. The win rate goes from 56.25% to 55.21%, a single point. That is closer to the starting score than any of the team's three unchanged replays, which landed between 52.34% and 53.12%. Measured over 72 move edits from tournament-ready teams, a move edit moves win rate by 4.84 points once luck is removed, so a single small result like this one says little about moves in general.

facts.claim: Edit a09_A1 changes Raichu's Nuzzle to Volt Tackle and nothing else.
a09_A1 scored 0.5521 over 384 battles. The starting team scored 0.5625, replays 0.5234, 0.5312 and 0.5286.
facts.source: ~/vgc-data/edit_kind_rerun/run/results/ruggedness_shuffled50.json, vgc.anchors[9].edits, file a09_A1.txt, and vgc.anchors[9].f and .reps

facts.claim: The move-edit size from tournament-ready teams is 4.84 points, interval 3.35 to 6.23, over 72 edits.
facts.source: ~/vgc-data/edit_kind_rerun/run/results/ruggedness2_shuffled50.json, vgc.meta.A_move_swap.delta_star and .edits; code/docs/ruggedness2.md, table in 'Reading without the 5-point cutoff'
